calleo.intro: Calleo is an audio guest book company: guests pick up a retro-style telephone, hear a recorded greeting and leave a voicemail, which Calleo edits into a keepsake recording. It covers weddings in England, Scotland and Wales, plus destination weddings abroad.
about: Calleo, a trading name of B R Ventures Ltd, was founded by Bailey and Rob and launched in 2022. Calleo says the idea came after Rob's grandfather, Bob Langley, died in 2021: Rob wished he could hear his grandfather's voice once more, which his handwritten guest book entry could not capture. The service offers an alternative to the written guest book, and Calleo suggests it for weddings, birthdays and any celebration.

Calleo describes itself as family-run. Bailey's parents, Sarah and Phil, handle the admin and prepare each phone once a booking is made. The process starts with an availability form; customers then choose a phone and package and pay in full by debit or credit card or Klarna. A welcome pack follows, and customers record a custom greeting, though the CORE package excludes a personalised greeting.

The phone arrives by courier two days before the event. It needs no Wi-Fi or landline, only a standard 13 amp socket, and Calleo recommends placing it at least five metres from bands, DJs or speakers. After the event, it is returned at a post office, while the ELEGANT package includes collection by Calleo staff. Calleo cannot ship to Northern Ireland.

Calleo says it listens to and edits every voicemail. Customers review a first-draft MP3 in an online gallery and can request changes within their package's allowance before approving any USB, vinyl record or video memory book. Calleo's company policies page links its public liability insurance and PAT certificates, and its homepage displays a 2024 Wedding Industry Awards regional winner badge.

services.name: Audio guest book phone hire
services.description: Retro phones in six styles (Dahlia, Lily, Poppy, Bluebell, Fern and Pearl), with choice depending on package. They need no Wi-Fi or landline, just a 13 amp socket; guests can leave unlimited voicemails.
services.more: Calleo's terms ask hirers to check the phone as soon as it arrives and report any defect straight away, as 24 hours after delivery it is taken to be in good order. Calleo provides support if a problem arises while it is in use.

services.more: CORE uses the Dahlia, Lily or Poppy phone with a digital PDF instruction sign and one chance to remove voicemails. ESSENTIAL adds the Bluebell phone, a non-personalised sign and an engraved USB, while ELEVATED opens up every phone except the King, Duchess and Duke, adds a personalised sign and allows up to five new voicemails to be added.

services.name: ELEGANT package
services.description: At £1,399 it includes any phone, the Lilibet Telephone Box stand, a hand-crafted sign, set-up and collection by Calleo staff, a five-day turnaround, unlimited revisions and a vinyl record or video memory book.
services.more: Any phone in the range is included, the vintage King, Duchess and Duke among them. Calleo describes it as the ideal way to add a touch of luxury to an event.

services.description: The King (antique brass rotary), Duchess (vintage white) and Duke (vintage black) phones. Calleo says any of them can be added to its packages for an extra £100.
services.more: The £100 upgrade applies to the CORE, ESSENTIAL and ELEVATED packages; ELEGANT already includes any phone.

services.name: Keepsake presentations
services.description: Beyond the edited MP3, ESSENTIAL adds an engraved USB; ELEVATED and ELEGANT offer a video memory book, pairing photos or video with the voicemails, or a custom-artwork vinyl record of up to 30 minutes.
services.more: Every package includes the compiled MP3 file. Engraved USBs can be designed with up to 10 options, from font styles to personal text, and for the video book Calleo works with the couple's photo or video team.

services.name: Destination wedding hire
services.description: A Dahlia or Lily phone with ESSENTIAL features, posted two days before UK departure and carried in checked luggage. Calleo gives an approximate cost of £338 for the first weekend plus £100 per extra weekend.
services.more: The phone travels in a travel bag supplied by Calleo, about 20cm x 15cm and 2kg. Calleo notes that most couples arrange for a family member or friend to travel with the phone to keep costs down.

howItWorks.title: Check your date
howItWorks.text: Send the form on Calleo's website to see if your date is free, then pick a phone and package and book by paying in full through a secure payment link.

howItWorks.title: Get ready
howItWorks.text: A detailed welcome pack explains what happens next. You record the greeting guests will hear when they lift the handset, and depending on your package Calleo personalises the instruction sign.

howItWorks.title: Delivery and set-up
howItWorks.text: A courier brings the phone to the address of your choice two days ahead of the event. Plug it in, give it a few minutes to warm up and place it away from loud noise.

howItWorks.title: Send it back
howItWorks.text: After the event, the phone goes back through the post office on the agreed return date, using the pre-paid label.

howItWorks.title: Listen and finalise
howItWorks.text: Calleo compiles and edits the recordings into a first-draft MP3 within your package's turnaround, counted from one working day after the phone arrives back. Once you have made any changes your package allows, the final keepsake is personalised and produced.

goodToKnow.text: The phone needs a small table or surface of about 30cm x 40cm in a quieter spot, plugged into a mains 13 amp socket. It can be used indoors, or outside if covered, but not in an area used as an entrance or emergency exit route.

Someone must be at the agreed address to accept delivery, though it does not have to be the customer. The phone must go back in its original shipping box, and the hirer is responsible for loss, theft or damage from delivery until it is returned.

Calleo's terms place responsibility for getting guests to leave messages on the customer; no refund is given if fewer messages are recorded than hoped, though Calleo recommends ways to encourage plenty.

Recordings are stored for up to two years and then deleted. On written request, Calleo will not use them for other purposes such as marketing, and will securely delete or return the audio files when the agreement ends.
Turnaround times can occasionally be extended, which the terms ask customers to accept.
Calleo says its phones can be fully booked months in advance.

faqs.q: What does the phone need at the venue?
faqs.a: Just a standard 13 amp power socket. It works without Wi-Fi or a landline connection.

faqs.q: How do guests leave a message?
faqs.a: Once plugged in, the phone takes a few minutes to warm up. Guests then pick up the handset, hear your recorded greeting and leave a message after the beep. A framed how-to-use guide is provided for guests.

faqs.q: Can the phone go near the band or DJ?
faqs.a: Calleo recommends keeping it at least 5 metres from loud sound sources such as bands, singers, DJs and speakers. They review recordings and reduce background noise as much as possible, but the phone should not sit right next to a speaker.

faqs.q: Do they cover Northern Ireland?
faqs.a: No. Because of logistical constraints Calleo cannot ship to Northern Ireland; it covers weddings in England, Scotland and Wales, plus destination weddings.

faqs.q: How soon do we receive the recordings?
faqs.a: The digital audio guest book arrives in 21 days on the CORE and ESSENTIAL packages, 10 days on ELEVATED and 5 days on ELEGANT.

faqs.q: Can we change our date or cancel?
faqs.a: Under Calleo's hire terms, rescheduling is free if requested no later than 15 weeks before the hire period and costs 35% of the invoice within that window. Cancelling no later than 15 weeks ahead brings a 25% refund; after that there is no refund.

faqs.q: Can we take a phone to a wedding abroad?
faqs.a: Yes. Calleo sends a Dahlia or Lily phone by Royal Mail two days before UK departure. It must travel in checked luggage, not in cabin bags, and is returned via the post office on the agreed date with the label provided. For a detailed quote, Calleo asks couples to get in touch.

cj-sax.tagline: Based in London, creating vibes worldwide…
cj-sax.intro: CJ SAX LIVE is the business of CJ, who describes himself as a London-based saxophonist, DJ and event planner. He offers live sax and sax-and-DJ sets for weddings, corporate events and parties in the UK and abroad.
about: His website's name describes wedding sax and DJ work in London alongside event planning and entertainment in Essex. Under the line 'Based in London, creating vibes worldwide…', its Destinations section highlights Ibiza (Ushuaia), the Amalfi Coast (Villa Cimbrone), D'Maris Bay (Nusr'et Restaurant) and Cape Town (MolenVliet Vineyard).

His website and press pack say CJ has performed at the London 2012 Olympics and at the Abu Dhabi and Monaco F1 Grand Prix. They also name venues such as The O2, the Tower of London, The Dorchester and Ronnie Scott's, along with performances in Ibiza, Dubai, Marbella, Cannes and Mallorca. According to the press pack, he launched his own events company and works with high-profile clients, and the business says it has provided event services for over a decade.

With the live sax option, CJ plays alongside the client's own DJ, while the combined sax-and-DJ act brings his own sound system and lighting. His DJ sets are open format and aim to read the crowd, running from 70s and 80s soul through club classics, house, dance anthems, old-school RnB and garage. The business also recommends performers from its network, such as DJs, bongo players, violinists and a magician, and helps coordinate them.

CJ's own packages include public liability insurance, an event contract and invoice, and WhatsApp support. His pricing calendar treats May to September (worldwide) and November to December (London) as peak periods. January to April and October (Dubai and London) are off-peak, and discounted off-peak prices are available on enquiry, subject to availability.

grape-fig.tagline: THE HOME OF 100% BRITISH, ARTISAN CHEESE & CHARCUTERIE, STYLED BEAUTIFULLY
grape-fig.intro: GRAPE & Fig is a sister-run grazing company based in Romford. They make sharing platters, grazing tables and on-site food displays centred on 100% British cheese and charcuterie, with ready-to-eat orders hand-delivered to most of the M25 area and Essex.
about: Toria Smith founded the company in 2017. While planning her own wedding the year before, she had wanted a four-metre grazing table to serve as canapés and starters combined. The business says it brought the concept of 'grazing' to the UK from Australia. Her sister Catherine joined in spring 2019, and together they cater for gatherings, celebrations and brand events.

Since the start of 2022 they have used only British cheese and charcuterie, sourced from small dairy farms and independent artisan producers across the UK. Every cheese or charcuterie-based platter comes with a menu and a map showing where the produce is from. The business says everything is handmade each morning in its kitchens with locally sourced, seasonal produce. The team are also trained florists and combine food and flowers in their displays.

Hand-deliveries are made by their own same-day, fragile-goods courier service from Tuesday to Saturday, with a £130 minimum spend, and orders can also be collected from their HQ. They prefer as much notice as possible but need only 48 hours for last-minute orders, though days can close once capacity is reached. Selected gift boxes, kits and hampers ship overnight to most of mainland UK.

In April 2024 the business opened what it calls the UK's first 'Build Your Own British Cheese Box Bar' on London's Regent Street. At the launch, customers chose a box size and a base of cheese, charcuterie or vegan cheese, added condiments and built the box alongside the team. Its website advertises the bar as a seasonal summer pop-up at Brityard, 285 Regent Street.

goodToKnow.text: Local delivery runs Tuesday to Saturday. Standard delivery (8am–5pm) is £15; a morning window (8am–12pm) is standard delivery plus £25, an afternoon window (12pm–4pm) is standard delivery plus £5, and a chosen two-hour window between 6am and 4pm is standard delivery plus £55 or £60, depending on the window.

Deliveries are made strictly to the ground floor (front door, concierge or building reception) or to a loading bay, which must be pre-booked if the building requires it. If there is nowhere safe and legal to unload outside, someone needs to meet the courier.

The person who placed the order should be there to receive it and check everything on arrival. Missing, incorrect or damaged items must be reported at the point of delivery, with photos, before the order is accepted.
Delivery details can be changed within a two-hour grace period after booking; after that, the delivery window and address cannot be changed.

If no one is available and there is no safe place to leave the order, the courier waits up to 10 minutes; re-delivery, where possible, costs £25. Any parking charges the courier has to pay are passed on to the customer.

Ready-to-eat food is freshly prepared on the day of delivery or collection and is best enjoyed that day. Platters are delicate, must be kept perfectly flat, and anything that needs chilling should go straight into the fridge.
UK shipping needs a £50 minimum spend.

Overnight UK shipping, usually by DHL, is available for selected products and arrives Tuesday to Thursday between 8am and 8pm (later in busy periods). The chilled packaging keeps items food-safe for at least 24 hours.

faqs.q: How far in advance should we order?
faqs.a: As early as possible. They need only 48 hours' notice for last-minute orders, but some days close once they reach capacity, so ordering ahead avoids disappointment.

faqs.q: Where do they deliver?
faqs.a: Most of the M25 area and Essex. The full postcode list is on their Delivery Policy page, and you can also check your postcode at checkout. If you are just outside the area, they may be able to help depending on availability, or you can arrange your own courier to collect from their HQ.

faqs.q: Can we collect the order ourselves?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose collection at checkout; collections from the Romford HQ run Tuesday to Saturday, 9am–10am, and must be made within the booked slot.

faqs.q: Can we add items after ordering?
faqs.a: They will always try to fit in last-minute additions, depending on availability, so get in touch as soon as possible. Pantry, drinks and serveware items can also be added to an existing order.

faqs.q: Should the platter stay in its box?
faqs.a: Either works. Each platter is arranged on a wooden board that can be lifted out to serve, or it can be kept in its branded box. Several platters lined up together give a grazing-table effect.

faqs.q: How should cheese platters be served?
faqs.a: Store them cold but do not serve them cold: take them out of the fridge one to two hours before serving for the best flavour.

faqs.q: How are allergies and dietary needs handled?
faqs.a: Add any allergy or dietary requirements at the basket stage. Every platter comes with an allergy notice card and a menu listing the relevant allergens.

harry-de-cruz.tagline: Modern Magic, designed to be remembered.
harry-de-cruz.intro: Harry De Cruz is a magician, mind reader and event host based in London and New York. He offers close-up, stage and wedding magic, parlour shows and compèring for corporate events, product launches, private parties and weddings.
about: He combines a background in stand-up comedy with technical sleight of hand and mentalism, and performs in a relaxed, conversational style. He says he has over 15 years of experience performing at events and is available worldwide, and that he has worked in more than 30 countries, from product launches in the United States to private dinners across Europe and celebrations in the Maldives.

Harry says he has performed at hundreds of weddings and plans the timing of the magic with each couple, whether that means mingling at the drinks reception, going from table to table at the wedding breakfast or performing in the evening. Before clients book, he offers to meet them for a coffee or over Zoom, free of charge, and show them some magic.

Alongside his event work, he says he co-wrote and performs in the magic show AMAZE at New World Stages in New York. His homepage also lists Wonderville at The Palace Theatre in London's West End and Champions of Magic at the Boulevard Theatre among his theatre shows, without saying whether those runs are current. Behind the scenes, he works as a creative advisor, writer and designer for magicians and theatre shows.

The credits he lists include Magic Director and Resident Director on Derren Brown's Unbelievable, and 'the better part of a decade' with Dynamo, including as Head of Magic. He describes himself as an award-winning London magician, and his website says he was awarded London Magician of the Year in 2024, 2025 and 2026. A 2022 profile in Absolutely Magazine describes him as born and raised in Buckinghamshire, says he joined The Magic Circle at 18 and names him as an Associate of the Inner Magic Circle.

services.name: Close-up and roaming magic
services.description: Conversational, intimate magic performed right in guests' hands, often with their own belongings, as Harry mingles between groups or gives a mini show at the table.
services.more: He pitches it as the chance to see the kind of tricks people are sceptical of on television, up close and in their own hands. The aim is to give guests something to laugh about, talk about and share together.

services.name: Stage and after-dinner magic
services.description: Interactive stage performances of modern magic, mind reading and British humour, for anything from an intimate private room to a large theatre. He says his stage magic can play to hundreds or thousands of people.
services.more: Some routines involve everyone in the room at once, creating a reaction on a scale he says you will not have seen before.

services.name: Wedding magic
services.description: Magic planned with each couple. Common slots are the drinks reception, table to table between courses at the wedding breakfast, the turnover before evening guests arrive, and the evening reception.
services.more: Between courses at the wedding breakfast, his table-to-table sets are designed as an ice-breaker and talking point for each table. At the evening reception he mixes and mingles between groups to round off the day.

services.name: Event hosting and compèring
services.description: Hosting and compèring an event to keep it moving and the energy up, with magic and mind reading placed in the transitions between parts of the programme.
services.more: He describes his hosting as reliable, relaxed and captivating: he keeps the event moving, makes each transition feel effortless and brings the room together.

services.name: Parlour show
services.description: An intimate, interactive show of magic and mind reading for small to medium groups, designed for a living room or private dining room.
services.more: It is designed for friends, family or colleagues gathered in one room, and the audience is involved throughout.

services.name: Bespoke brand magic
services.description: Custom magic built around a client's brand, campaign, message, slogan or product, drawing on his behind-the-scenes work as a magic consultant, writer and creator.
services.more: Behind the scenes he has created, written and directed magic for internationally recognised performers, major West End productions and global brand campaigns. He brings that experience to original pieces designed for a specific event, audience or brand.

faqs.a: Anywhere you like. He is based between London and New York and is available worldwide.

faqs.q: Why book a magician?
faqs.a: He says the answer depends on the event. Magic can break the ice for a group of people who have not met before, or be a surprise addition to a dinner party, and either way it gives everyone a shared experience of wonder.

faqs.q: How large an audience can he perform for?
faqs.a: His parlour show is designed for small to medium groups in a living room or private dining room. His stage magic suits audiences of hundreds or thousands and can be scaled to fit any size of stage or theatre.

faqs.q: What is 'the turnover' at a wedding?
faqs.a: It is the gap between the wedding meal and the evening guests arriving. He suggests using it to keep the energy going into the evening and to welcome new arrivals with a surprise.

faqs.q: Will he tell us how the tricks work?

jamie-roche.intro: Jamie Roche is an Irish-born, London-based singer/songwriter whose live sets on guitar and vocals mix his own songs with folk songs and covers. His style is described as heavily influenced by artists such as Ray LaMontagne and Van Morrison.
about: His own songs include 'The Tide', with lyrics by Jamie Roche and Luke Carey. A live performance of it filmed at Painter Studios in London was shared in 2019, and 'The Tide (Acoustic)' followed in September 2022 on Orange Tree Records. 'Play The Fool', released on 23 October 2026 and also on Orange Tree Records, credits Jamie on vocals with Kealan Kenny as studio producer.

He grew up in North London, and his YouTube channel gathers live performances filmed around the city. They include Eric Bogle's 'The Green Fields of France' at St Mary Magdalene Church, Enfield, with Eilish Byrne-Whelehan on violin; Ray LaMontagne's 'Such a Simple Thing' at St John's Church, Hoxton; Chris Isaak's 'Wicked Game' at Sixty Sixty Sounds in Soho; and Fleetwood Mac's 'Dreams' at the Chinese Pagoda in Victoria Park, Hackney. Together they give a clear sense of his sound before an enquiry.

lucy-jane-cakes.intro: Lucy Jane Cakes is a cake maker whose TikTok bio gives London as its base and whose baker PEOPLE has called a buttercream specialist. Its videos show heart, character, photo and bento cakes; orders are taken by Instagram message.
about: In February 2025 PEOPLE reported that she had baked her entire life and began selling cakes professionally in 2016. The same article reported that she made seven cakes for her own wedding in London on 7 December 2024: a three-tier classic vanilla sponge as the main cake and six others, each a different flavour, with all seven finished two days before the wedding. She also told the story of making them in a TikTok video.

Alongside finished cakes, the TikTok account @lucy_jane_cakes has posted baking and decorating how-to videos. These include a photo-cake tutorial that names the Wilton 199 and Jen 2ES nozzles she used, along with tips on getting a level rise in 6-inch PME tins and on freezing leftover cake slices.

Her video captions use hashtags for both London and Essex, including #londoncakes, #lambethcake, #southwoodford and #essexcakes. Lucy Jane Cakes does not appear to have its own website and publishes no prices. Its TikTok bio says 'Message on Instagram for orders', and the account to message about an event cake is @lucy_jane_cakes.

magpie-catering.intro: Magpie Catering is an events catering company based in Hastingwood, Essex, serving the South East of England. They cater weddings, corporate functions, private dinners and celebrations at any venue, marquee or private home, from delivered buffets to fully staffed, managed events.
about: Managing Director Elizabeth Joyce says the business grew out of a restaurant she part-owned with her father, and that she started by catering small weddings and events such as funerals; the business names that restaurant as The Magpies Nest Restaurant in Epping. Magpie Catering describes itself as a professional events catering service, and the occasions it now caters extend to birthdays and christenings as well as funerals.

They bring all the catering equipment needed. Seated menus include qualified chefs, a personal events manager, waiting staff, cutlery, china and table laying, and their waiting staff are trained in-house and work in uniform. Weddings and larger events are offered a tasting beforehand, and regular corporate clients can ask for a sample buffet.

They describe their menus as globally influenced, drawing on English, Asian, Italian and French cooking with a modern approach, and say they research new products at trade and food shows to keep up with trends. Styles run from canapés and bowl food to finger and fork buffets, seated meals, BBQs, Turkish-inspired mezze and private fine dining, with gluten- and dairy-free options on several menus.

Case studies on their website include the Alleyn Court Preparatory School Summer Ball 2010 in Southend-on-Sea, with a champagne and canapé reception and a three-course dinner for 224 guests; marquee weddings, one of them at Ingatestone Hall; a seated wedding at Sutton Hall Farm, Rochford; and a 2009 venue-opening lunch in Beaconsfield, where canapés and bowl food were served to 170 guests.

services.name: Wedding catering
services.description: Personalised menus from canapés and a three-course sit-down meal to evening buffets, with glassware, tableware and linen options, a menu tasting and full event management. Themes range from English country garden to modern contemporary.
services.more: Wedding menus include a pre-ordered choice for guests, a children's menu at a reduced rate and full laying up of the room or marquee, down to name cards, candles and petals. Evening food runs from a lay-and-leave cheese and pâté counter to bagel, street-food, deli and BBQ menus.

services.name: Corporate event catering
services.description: Catering for meetings, working lunches, gala balls, product launches, AGMs and client entertaining, from delivered finger buffets to canapé receptions, bowl food and seated meals, with help on planning and logistics.
services.more: Corporate finger-buffet menus include a Healthy Finger Menu and a gluten- and dairy-free menu, with front-of-house staff available if required. Hog roasts are also among the corporate formats.

services.name: Seated meals and gala dinners
services.description: Bespoke three-course seated menus for summer balls, gala and corporate dinners, with a canapé selection, gluten- and dairy-free alternatives, a personal events manager, waiting staff and a full kitchen team.
services.more: Guests pre-order from two starters, three mains and two desserts (or one trio of desserts) across Menu Options A, B and C. Option C's fillet steak main is listed '@ £4.00 per person extra', and pricing is based on events of 60 guests, with a bespoke quotation for numbers above or below.

services.name: Canapés and bowl food
services.description: Hot and cold canapés and sweet finger desserts, cooked by a personal chef and served by uniformed staff, plus bowl food for standing receptions, from meat and fish to vegetarian dishes and desserts.
services.more: Bowl food lets standing guests mingle as they would at a canapé reception while still having a satisfying meal, and Magpie is happy to talk through the concept to help choose a menu.

services.name: BBQs and Turkish mezze
services.description: BBQ menus, British-themed to Mediterranean, cooked in view of guests, with options including a burger station and Turkish shish station, plus a Turkish-inspired mezze menu of sharing boards, shish and baklava.
services.more: BBQ meat comes from a local supplier, and sharing starter boards, antipasti and a children's BBQ menu are among the options; a luxury cheese platter is available at an additional charge. The mezze menu includes a vegetable moussaka as its vegetarian main.

services.name: Private dining and celebrations
services.description: Private dinner parties at home for six or more, with a personal chef and one of their waiting staff, plus menus for birthdays, anniversaries, reunions and garden parties in a home, marquee or hired venue.
services.more: For dinner parties, an executive chef first advises on exact requirements for the evening. For other celebrations, Magpie can advise which food style suits the occasion, from cocktail parties to hog roasts, and help with plans and logistics.

howItWorks.title: Share your brief
howItWorks.text: Tell Magpie your exact requirements and menu preferences, and they will put together a quotation based on your event's details.

howItWorks.title: Taste the menu
howItWorks.text: For weddings, the chosen three-course menu is cooked in full for the couple at Magpie's catering studio in Hastingwood, so presentation, portion size and equipment can be agreed early.

howItWorks.title: Secure the booking
howItWorks.text: A 25% non-refundable deposit secures a delivered finger buffet. After a wedding tasting, the deposit falls due two weeks after the tasting date.

howItWorks.title: Confirm final numbers
howItWorks.text: For finger buffets, the balance and final guest numbers are due by BACS two weeks before the event.

goodToKnow.text: Delivery is free within 7 miles of Magpie's kitchens; beyond that it is charged at 85p per mile.

Delivered buffets arrive garnished on disposable black platters, with matching black plates and napkins offered '@ 35p'. China, wood and slate platters with china plates carry a 50p per person supplement plus an 85p-per-mile round-trip collection charge, and the client is responsible for hired equipment when Magpie's staff are not on site.

When staff are booked, china, wood and slate platters and china plates are included. Waiting and drinks staff are charged at £12.50 p/h and wear white shirts, black bistro aprons, black ties and black trousers with name badges.
Food temperatures are logged when deliveries leave the unit and when they arrive, and Magpie recommends delivered food is not left out for more than 3.5 hours.
Wedding menu pricing is based on events of over 40 guests, with a bespoke quotation for smaller numbers.

Wedding menus exclude linen, cooking equipment (for 100 guests or under: two six-burner gas ovens with gas, an electric urn and a deep fat fryer), a cake stand and knife, wine coolers, table number stands, drinks fridges, ice and after-dinner bar service. Linen and bar service can be quoted on request.
New corporate clients settle their first invoice before the event; after that, payment is due by BACS seven days after the invoice date.
All prices in Magpie's brochure are subject to VAT at the current rate.
Menus may be amended at the last minute, subject to availability.

faqs.q: What is the minimum order for a delivered buffet?
faqs.a: Delivered finger buffets have a minimum order of 15 guests. They arrive freshly prepared, garnished and ready to serve.

faqs.q: How much notice does a corporate lunch need?
faqs.a: Magpie asks for three working days' notice but says it will always try to accommodate a last-minute order. Changes or cancellations must be emailed and phoned through before 10am the morning before, or the order is charged in full. The minimum order is £42.50.

faqs.q: Can they cater for dietary requirements?
faqs.a: Yes. Wedding menus include a dietary/allergen option, for example gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free or for lactose intolerance, and Magpie asks to be told if halal, organic or dairy-free food is needed. Allergen information is available on request.

faqs.q: Can we taste the wedding menu first?
faqs.a: Yes. Magpie offers a free full tasting of the chosen menu at its catering studio in Hastingwood. It is complimentary for the couple at weddings over 60 guests, with a charge for extra guests, and a per-person charge plus VAT applies if the booking is not confirmed afterwards.

faqs.q: Is drinks service included at a wedding?
faqs.a: Wedding menus include glassware and beverage staff for the reception drinks and the meal, up to the speeches. After-dinner drinks service and bar equipment can be quoted separately.

faqs.q: Can they feed our other suppliers?
faqs.a: Yes. Supplier meal options are available for photographers, videographers, bands, DJs and similar.

faqs.q: Can they cater a funeral at short notice?
faqs.a: Yes. Magpie says it is readily available at short notice for funerals, with menus designed for these occasions, and can also arrange drinks and drinks service, glassware, linen and setting up and clearing the hall.

meatstop.intro: Meat Stop is an Essex-born burger business offering BBQ and burger catering for weddings, corporate events and parties across Essex, with two London locations listed on its website: The Commercial Tavern in Shoreditch and Hand of Glory in Dalston.
about: The business explains that its line 'fast food, upgraded.' means better ingredients, in-house recipes and custom-spec brioche buns rather than bigger portions. It says it keeps the menu tight, cooks everything fresh and uses dry-aged beef farmed in its home county of Essex, ground fresh for its burgers. Meat Stop describes itself as 'Essex-born. London-serving. Premium fast food.'

For events, Meat Stop says it has gone 'back to our roots; the garden BBQ'. It also says it has over 20 years of experience in catering, event planning and preparing food, and offers to do the heavy lifting so hosts can sit back and enjoy their event. Its catering page names Essex towns including Colchester, Chelmsford, Southend, Basildon, Billericay, Epping and Maldon, and invites enquiries for an accurate quote.

The business has its roots in Brentwood, Essex. In 2015 its website described Meat Stop as Brentwood's only boutique burger bar, serving dine-in and takeaway from Crown Street, and named Benjamin as its chef and founder. A Burger Dudes review published in July 2026 reports that Meat Stop opened at The Commercial Tavern by the end of 2025, and that the reviewers tried its burgers at Burger Fest UK 2026.

services.more: On its supplier profile, Meat Stop says its event food is built on dry-aged beef, house-made sauces and locally baked brioche buns. It describes a professional set-up for corporate events, works with couples on wedding receptions, and uses a compact, high-output set-up for festivals and pop-ups.

natalie-max.intro: Natalie & Max Photo and Films is a husband-and-wife wedding photography and videography duo based in Ware, Hertfordshire. They cover weddings from preparations to party across Hertfordshire, Essex and the wider UK, as well as destination weddings abroad.
about: Natalie and Max met at university, where they studied photography and design. They say they started photographing weddings together in 2012, the year they set up the business. After graduating they moved to the Algarve to live and work, and they now describe themselves as a British duo who spend half the year in the UK and the rest in the Algarve, where they married in 2022.

Their aim is to blend in like 'one of the guests', and they sum up what they do as 'Two guests with great cameras'. On the day they usually arrive at bridal preparations about two hours before the couple leaves for the ceremony, and stay until around 30 minutes after the first dance. Photographs are delivered within four to six weeks and films within six to eight weeks, through a private online gallery.

They say they take a maximum of 35 weddings a year, including destination weddings, and that couples usually book 12 to 18 months ahead. Their terms ask for a non-refundable 30% deposit to secure a date, and UK travel beyond 30 miles of Ware is charged at £1 per mile. Alongside weddings they shoot fashion and editorial work; their editorial page says they are the official photographers and videographers for wedding dress designers Ivory & Co and Dress Me Pretty.

services.name: Wedding photography
services.description: Full-day photography from prep to party with one photographer, including a one-to-one consultation, a customised wedding-day timeline, edited images, printed and mounted photographs and an online gallery with free downloads.
services.more: Their collections page lists the Photo Collection at £2300, with one photographer covering the day from prep to party, five complimentary printed and mounted photographs and travel within a 30-mile radius. The one-to-one consultation can be held at their office or online.

services.name: Wedding videography
services.description: Full-day filming with one videographer and professional audio recording, producing a highlight film of five to ten minutes that couples can access and share online.
services.more: Their collections page lists the Films Collection at £2200, covering the day from prep to party with one videographer. It includes a one-to-one consultation online or at their office and travel within a 30-mile radius.

services.name: Signature Collections (photo and film)
services.description: One photographer and one videographer cover the whole day, discounted for booking both together. The Signature Collection Plus adds drone coverage and a 'movie style' feature film of up to 90 minutes.
services.more: Their collections page describes the Signature Collections as their most popular collections. Both include a highlight video of five to ten minutes, ten complimentary printed photographs and travel within a 30-mile radius.

services.name: Destination weddings
services.description: They photograph and film weddings abroad as well as in the UK, listing the Algarve, the South of France, the Greek Islands, Italy, Sicily, Spain, Thailand and America among their destinations.
services.more: Their portfolio features destination weddings at venues including Domaine d'Essendiéras and Chateau Lacanaud in France, Castillo de Viñuelas in Spain, Torre San Marco on Lake Garda and VidaMar in the Algarve. They say they take only a limited number of weddings each year so that every couple gets their undivided attention.

services.name: Wedding albums
services.description: Four styles: The Frame, which fits inside a photo frame; The Flush, in materials such as leather or linen; The Mounted, with ivory mounts; and The Signature, a digital album that plays the wedding video.
services.more: The Frame, their most popular album, comes in landscape, portrait or square formats in four sizes and can hold anywhere from 40 to 400 photos. The Flush comes in six sizes with a rounded or square spine and an embossed, photo or plain cover, while The Mounted is recommended for 100 to 200 photographs. Their extras list a photo album at £550, and parent albums can be added when ordering.

services.name: Engagement shoots and extras
services.description: Add-ons include engagement or 'trash the dress' shoots on photo or film, an additional photographer, drone footage, a feature film of up to 90 minutes, and full-length ceremony, speeches and first-dance films.
services.more: Their collections page lists extras including an additional photographer, drone footage, an engagement shoot and a longer feature film; ask the business for current prices.

identity.note: The business formerly traded as New Pixels Photo + Film, and its start date is inconsistent: its About page gives 2012, its homepage says over 15 years, and other listings give 2006 or 2016.

howItWorks.text: Couples get in touch through the contact form or by arranging a video call to check availability and hear about the collections. Natalie and Max aim to reply within 24 hours.

goodToKnow.text: After the deposit, the remaining balance is invoiced in two equal instalments, and the final payment is due no later than 45 days before the wedding.

If a couple moves their date after paying the deposit and Natalie and Max are free on the new date, a further fee equal to 30% of the package price applies. If they are already booked on the new date, the change is treated as a cancellation.

For destination weddings, flights of up to £120 per person are included, based on travelling the day before and returning the day after; the couple pays any difference. Where a venue abroad is hard to reach by public transport, the couple covers car hire, while the duo cover their own accommodation in the UK and EU unless agreed otherwise in writing.
They ask to be the only professional photographer and videographer at the wedding, unless another arrangement is agreed with them in writing beforehand.
Couples confirm that they and their guests can be photographed and filmed, and should raise any concerns as early as possible.

Natalie and Max keep the copyright and may use wedding images and films for promotion. Couples can print and share their photos and films for personal use, but commercial use needs written agreement in advance.
Consultations take place at their office or online, and the photo and Signature collections include a customised wedding-day timeline. UK collections include travel within a 30-mile radius.
Albums can be ordered with a 10% deposit. After ordering, couples pick their photos through a link and approve a page-by-page layout before the album goes to print.

faqs.q: How does booking work?
faqs.a: First they check the date is still free, then they get to know the couple by phone or email. Once both sides agree it is a good fit, they send the details for securing the date with a 30% deposit, followed by a booking confirmation and a wedding guide.

faqs.q: When is the balance due?
faqs.a: The balance after the deposit is split into two equal instalments, and the final one must be paid no later than 45 days before the wedding. Deposits and instalments are non-refundable if the couple cancels.

faqs.q: What happens if we need to change our wedding date?
faqs.a: They will try to accommodate the new date. If they are free, an extra fee equal to 30% of the package price secures it; if they already have a booking that day, the change counts as a cancellation.

faqs.q: What if the photographer or videographer is ill on the day?
faqs.a: Their terms say that if either cannot attend through illness or other unforeseen circumstances, they will provide a suitable replacement.

faqs.q: Can another photographer or videographer work at our wedding too?

ozzy-stix.intro: Ozzy&Stix is an Essex-based duo of a vocalist and a guitarist, offering acoustic sets and party sets for weddings and parties. Both members also DJ, and clients can add a sax, violin or trumpet.
about: Alongside vocals and guitar, both members play bongos and percussion. Their website is focused on weddings, under the line 'We Create The Best Memories on Your Big Day', and they say they can provide music and entertainment from the ceremony through to the full party. Beyond the Essex base given on their contact page, the site's own description and 'LDN' logo also present them as a London duo.

As DJs, they say they are comfortable with Jewish dancing, Bhangra and plenty of other genres that may come up at weddings. Those extra instruments come through their #MADE offer, and their FAQ says further musicians and singers are available from their own books. They will also perform alongside other acts, including external DJs, if they feel the combination will work well.

They build sets from a guide to what the crowd enjoys and are happy to remove songs connected to bad memories. They will learn specific songs within reason, asking for at least six weeks' notice for a first dance or ceremony song. PAT test and public liability documents, and a repertoire list, are available on request. They do not provide lighting but may be able to suggest a supplier. They will travel abroad, with flights, accommodation and transfers paid by the client on top of the fee.

Previous clients named on their website include the V&A Museum London, Deutsche Bank, Just Seventy Events, London Rox Events, Royal Caribbean Cruises, Sunseeker Luxury Yachts, BNP Paribas and PHJR Events. They play a few public gigs each year and announce the dates on Instagram. Their YouTube channel has acoustic covers, mashups and an 'O&S Presents' session series, which give a feel for their sound.

paint-and-pour.intro: Paint & Pour runs guided sip-and-paint nights in Epping and Chingford, where founder Bryony takes guests through a painting step by step. No experience is needed, and every guest leaves with their finished canvas.
about: Bryony says she started Paint & Pour with a simple idea: most people haven't picked up a paintbrush since school, and they really should, preferably with a glass of wine in the other hand. Guests can come with friends, with a date or on their own.

Each night runs for three hours. Guests arrive, collect a complimentary drink and find an easel before Bryony starts them on the painting, with music playing. Canvas, paints, brushes and aprons are all provided, so guests only need to bring themselves. The evening closes with a 'Mini Gallery & Photo Time'.

Public nights take place at Carpino Lounge on Epping High Street and at The Royal Forest on Ranger's Road, Chingford. Tickets for the currently listed nights are sold through Eventbrite at £35 each; they are non-refundable, but Bryony offers a transfer to an event on another date. Doors open at 6:40pm, with check-in at 7pm and painting from 7:30pm. Under-18s must come with a parent or legal guardian.

The organiser says the events usually sell out and suggests following their Eventbrite page to hear about new dates first. Their public pages do not describe private or exclusive bookings, so anyone planning a group occasion should ask them directly, through Eventbrite or Instagram, about availability and format.

ray-johnson.intro: Ray Elton Johnson is an Essex-based Elton John tribute act, lookalike and singer, with television and film appearances as Elton. He performs at weddings, private parties and corporate events across East London, Essex, Kent, Hertfordshire and the M25 area.
about: Ray, also known as Elton Ray Johnson, has been in the business for 30 years, according to his site. The site gives his base as Theydon Bois on the homepage and Chigwell on the contact page. His television career began on an ITV series about the Derek's Doubles lookalike agency. His site says the series was sold to 39 countries, and afterwards he performed in New Zealand and several European countries.

He has since appeared on programmes including Ant & Dec's Saturday Night Takeaway, That Peter Kay Thing, Have I Got News For You, The Weakest Link, Jimmy Carr's Big Fat Wedding and Big Fat Quiz of Everything. He took part in LadBaby's 2022 Christmas No. 1, and body-doubled for Elton on the set of Charlotte Tilbury's 2023 Christmas promo.

His About page says he has appeared as Elton John in five films and names the French comedy God Save The Tuche (2025) as the latest. His site shares photos from the set in Lille. His gallery also mentions an appearance at An Evening with Chris Moyles and Dominic Byrne at the London Palladium in January 2026, as well as a performance at Firs Park Resort in Essex.

As well as his own shows, he plays a duo set in pubs and clubs with Nigel Silk, a drummer from the tribute band T Rexasy, and has started George 'n' Elton, a combined George Michael and Elton John tribute that opened at the Comrades Club in Clacton-on-Sea. His site says he is available for events 'from intimate pub gigs to grand weddings', with customisable performances. His FAQ recommends booking at least three months ahead.

the-bar-people.intro: The Bar People is a London-based mobile bar company serving events nationwide. They offer all-inclusive, dry hire and cash bars, staff hire and event management for corporate events, weddings, private parties and festivals.
about: Their bespoke pop-up bars are modular and can be customised for indoor or outdoor use, in any size or colour, with listed sizes running from 5ft up to a 40ft island. For corporate events they describe more than a decade of experience, offering signature cocktails, branded bar setups and interactive cocktail stations, plus eco-friendly options such as biodegradable straws and locally sourced ingredients. They handle everything from setup to cleanup.

For weddings, they provide bar service for a few hours or the whole day, with custom cocktail menus, themed setups, and wine and beer stations. Non-alcoholic drinks and mocktails can be added to any package, and all-inclusive packages include setup and takedown. Their cash bars are described as licensed to serve alcohol at any venue.

The business is run by The Bar People Limited (company number 12161824). Event management is handled as a team: Jake Lee looks after corporate events and logistics, and Kim Knight looks after private events and weddings. They recommend booking at least three months ahead, particularly for peak dates, and say they also cater for last-minute events. The 'We've Supported' section of their homepage shows brand logos including Salesforce, Sky, O2, EE and Batiste.

Each covers beer, wine and spirits, garnishes and consumables, plus a fridge, ice and glassware.

tl-executive-cars.intro: T&L Executive Cars is a private hire and chauffeur car service based in Theydon Bois, Essex. They provide wedding transport and guest transfers, corporate and special-event travel, and airport and cruise terminal transfers.
about: The business is also known as Theydon and Loughton Executive Cars. Its founder writes that he set it up in 2008 to serve local individuals and businesses, and that he personally guarantees the service to every customer. They say it was built on a professional, prompt and reliable service, and that over the years many of their clients have come to them through personal recommendation. They describe themselves as an alternative, affordable car service for local individuals, small businesses and corporate clients, including several multinational companies.

The fleet listed on their website is a Mercedes E Class and a Mercedes S Class (each for four passengers and three bags), a Mercedes V Class (seven passengers, seven bags) and a 'Toureno Custom Executive Spec' vehicle for eight passengers and eight bags. They say their vehicles are licensed and inspected by Epping Forest District Council and certificated as exempt from displaying a private hire plate, so journeys can be discreet, and they describe their drivers as smart and polite.

They serve Theydon Bois, Loughton, Epping, Abridge, Ongar, Buckhurst Hill, Chigwell and Woodford Green. Their listed hours are Monday to Friday, 9.00am to 6.30pm, and they say they reply within 24 hours. Quotes can be requested through an online form on their website, and accepted payment methods include Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Apple Pay.

services.more: The service is customised by working closely with each client and is offered at what the business calls an affordable price. Not displaying licensing logos helps present the professional image a business needs.

services.description: Keynote speaker transfers for several London speaking bureaux, plus logistical support for film and television shoots in London and the Home Counties; they say they are familiar with most red carpet events.

tm-event-hire.intro: TM Event Hire is an Essex marquee and event equipment hire company, supplying clear-span and pagoda marquees, mobile bars, furniture, catering equipment and tableware for weddings, parties, corporate functions and other private and public events across Essex, London and Hertfordshire.
about: The company is based in Barnston, Dunmow. According to the business, director Thomas Mclean founded it in 2013, initially specialising in catering equipment, tableware and glassware hire, and it previously traded as TM Catering Hire. His younger brother Michael Mclean joined in 2014 and became joint owner and chief of operations: Thomas looks after sales and customers, while Michael makes sure events are organised and equipment arrives on time.

The team delivers, sets up, de-rigs and collects seven days a week, and says its prices include delivery, setup and pickup. For marquees, the process starts with a site visit, and a 25% non-refundable deposit secures the booking. Equipment is installed one to three days before the event and collected the day after. Mobile bars are hired as equipment only, without alcohol or staff.

Beyond weddings and parties, they supply equipment for conferences, music festivals, awards ceremonies, fun fairs, farmers' markets and sporting events, as well as funeral and wake gatherings. They describe themselves as a member of the Event Hire Association with over 10 years of experience in the events, catering and wedding industries.

services.name: Clear-Span Marquee Hire
services.description: Modular marquees with no centre poles or guy ropes, suited to gardens, paving, shingle or decking. White or transparent walls, with options including festoon lights, carpet, transparent roofs, black-out ceilings and heaters.
services.more: The marquees are modular, so the size can be matched to the guest list, and doors are available to keep heat in on colder nights. For winter weddings, the business describes fully insulated marquees with heating options.

services.name: Chinese Hat (Pagoda) Marquee Hire
services.description: Curved-roof pagoda marquees with fabric linings, used alone for garden parties, doubled or tripled up, or added to a larger marquee as a catering tent or grand entrance. Dance floors, coconut matting and festoon lighting are available.
services.more: Pagodas have interchangeable PVC walls: solid white to keep a catering area out of view, or transparent sides for a summer garden party. They share the same specification as the clear-span marquees and can be used as entrance canopies, bar areas or seating spaces.

services.name: Mobile Bar Hire
services.description: LED straight, circular mirror, circular LED and wooden straight bars, with stools, glassware and refrigeration also available. Delivered the day before and collected the day after; equipment only, with no alcohol or staff.
services.more: Curved and straight bar sections can be mixed and matched. Bars can be tucked into marquee corners to free up dining and dancing space, or set up as a full-circle centrepiece. A full price list is available on request.

services.name: Furniture Hire
services.description: Limewash Chiavari and wooden folding chairs, round banquet and trestle tables, poser tables with stools, and white cubes, sofas, armchairs and coffee tables, delivered and collected across Essex, London and Hertfordshire.
services.more: Round banquet tables come in 3ft, 4ft, 5ft, 5.6ft and 6ft sizes and trestle tables in 4ft and 6ft, and a child's high chair is also available. Furniture hire fees include delivery before and collection after the event.

services.name: Kitchen Equipment & Tableware Hire
services.description: Industrial-grade catering equipment, including a six-ring gas oven, hot cupboard, gas BBQ, double fryer, drinks and bar fridges, water urn and chafing dishes, plus crockery, glassware and cutlery with a wash-up service (a 25% charge is added to tableware orders).
services.more: Published price lists show crockery from 30p per item (platters £2), glassware from 30p and cutlery from 27p, with serving pieces such as wine buckets at £2.95 and a metal cake stand at £7.00. Kitchen equipment ranges from a simple drinks-fridge set-up to a fully functional kitchen for a professional catering team; the hot cupboard runs on a 13amp supply.

services.name: Themed Event Packages
services.description: Themed hire packages for white, boho/rustic and Indian weddings, and for toddlers' parties, 18ths and 21sts, milestone birthdays and nightclub-style parties, plus small and large funeral and wake packages.
services.more: Package items are presented as a guide, and clients can add items or pick and choose between packages, although some items are not interchangeable. The large funeral and wake package suits guest lists of up to 200, and a garden marquee package for baby showers is also offered.

howItWorks.title: Request a quote
howItWorks.text: The online quote form asks for guest numbers, event type, address, date and preferred linings, lighting, flooring, dance floor, furniture, bar and extras. TM Event Hire says it emails a detailed quote within 24 hours, with all prices subject to a site visit.

howItWorks.title: Site visit
howItWorks.text: The team visits the site to assess the location and terrain, guest list size and event theme, so it can advise on what will work best.

howItWorks.title: Deposit
howItWorks.text: Any changes to the quote are agreed at this stage. If everything is agreeable, a 25% non-refundable deposit is invoiced to secure the booking.

howItWorks.title: Installation
howItWorks.text: The team delivers and puts up the equipment one to three days before the event.

howItWorks.title: Sign-off
howItWorks.text: Once everything is set up, the team leaves after the client gives final sign-off.

howItWorks.title: Collection
howItWorks.text: The team returns the next day to take down and collect the equipment.

goodToKnow.text: Final guest numbers are needed two weeks before the event. TM Event Hire recommends ordering as many chairs as guests invited, and says it always allows for numbers to rise or fall slightly.

Marquee lights and heaters run on low power, so a nearby house or building is usually enough. Caterers and bands may need a generator, which the team can quote for through one of its recommended suppliers.
On concrete or decking, marquees are held down with water barrels, and wooden flooring is recommended because carpet and matting are not suitable on those surfaces.
As a rule of thumb, the business's marquee guide suggests allowing about 10–12 sq ft per guest for a seated event, and slightly less for a standing or cocktail-style event.
If a venue will not allow set-up before the day, furniture can be delivered on the day of the event and collected that evening, for an out-of-hours charge.

Hired furniture can be dressed with drapes, but nothing should be pinned to it. Some furniture is weatherproof, and limewash chairs are fine for outdoor ceremonies in dry weather, but a cleaning charge applies if chairs are left outside and it rains.
Glasses are hired by the box rather than individually, and the published tableware price lists state that a 25% washing-up charge is added to the total tableware order.
Peak summer dates can sell quickly, while early- and late-season dates are often available at much shorter notice.
Package contents are a guide. Items can be added, and clients can mix items between packages, but some items may not be removable or interchangeable.
Flooring is included as part of the marquee hire service, with wooden flooring, carpet and coconut matting options, and outdoor walkways can be added to protect lawns and keep guests on a dry path.

faqs.q: How much does a marquee cost?
faqs.a: It depends on guest numbers, the extras chosen and the proposed location. TM Event Hire asks for full event details so it can prepare a detailed quote, and all prices are subject to a site visit.

faqs.q: How long does a marquee take to put up?
faqs.a: That depends on the size of the marquee and any extras. The team advises on timings when the booking is made, and installs equipment one to three days before the event.

faqs.q: Can a marquee go on a patio, concrete or decking?
faqs.a: Yes. The only difference is that the team supplies water barrels to secure the marquee, and wooden flooring is recommended because carpet and matting are not suitable on hard surfaces.

faqs.q: How is a marquee kept warm?
faqs.a: Indirect heaters sit outside the tent and blow warm air in through ducts, under thermostatic control. The team advises how many are needed for the marquee size and time of year.

faqs.q: Will we need a generator?
faqs.a: The marquee's lights and heaters run on low power, so a nearby house or building is a sufficient supply. Catering and bands may need a generator, and TM Event Hire can quote for one through a recommended supplier.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a Chinese hat and a marquee?
faqs.a: Very little in construction: they share the same specification and design, which is why they can be joined to a marquee. The difference is the curved, peaked shape, which gives a more elegant look.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book?
faqs.a: There is no fixed lead time. Peak summer dates can go quickly, while early- and late-season dates are often available at much shorter notice.

faqs.q: Can we decorate the hired furniture?
faqs.a: Within reason. Drapes to suit the theme are encouraged, but items must not be pinned, damaged or structurally altered.

tony-poole-discos.intro: Tony Poole Discos is a team of wedding, party and corporate event DJs based in Theydon Bois, Essex. As well as mobile discos, they supply uplighting, LED dance floors, backdrops, light-up LOVE letters, and photo and 360 video booths across Essex, Herts, London and beyond.
about: The business says it has been in the DJ industry for over 30 years and plays at venues across London and the Home Counties, and that its London venues have included Buckingham Palace, Grosvenor House, The Dorchester, The Ritz and The Shard. Its DJs page lists a team of 20, including Tony Poole and Richard Poole.

Tony Poole Discos describes its DJs as versatile and says they personalise each occasion, mixing requests with tracks they know will work. Before the day, clients are asked to send the tracks and genres they want played, plus a list of tracks or types of music they don't want played. On the night, the DJ reads the room and does their best to fit in guests' requests.

According to the business, every booking comes with an experienced DJ who co-ordinates and comperes moments such as the First Dance, a surprise entrance, announcements and introductions. Live entertainment can also be arranged. The business states that its sound and lighting equipment is PAT tested and complies with health and safety rules, and that it holds Public Liability Insurance. It adds that it has backup DJs and breakdown cover on its vehicles in case of emergencies.

To book, event details go onto a reservation form, which the client confirms by email. A 25% deposit is generally due within 14 days, with the balance paid on the night by cash or cheque, or in advance by BACS. Deposits are normally non-refundable but can be moved to another event.

services.name: Wedding DJs & All Day Service
services.description: A wedding DJ with an optional All Day Service. It covers set-up before guests arrive, background music for the drinks reception and meal, compering and wireless microphones for the speeches, and ceremony music through a mini PA.
services.more: Because the DJ is already set up, the party can start as soon as the speeches end. Background music through the drinks reception and meal can also run alongside a singer or musician, and the business says many of its DJs have radio credentials.

services.name: Corporate, Christmas & New Year's Eve DJs
services.description: DJs for corporate parties, dinner dances and awards nights, Christmas parties booked by companies and organisations, and venue or agency party nights. They also play New Year's Eve events at hotels, clubs, pubs and private residences.
services.more: The business says companies, clubs, associations, schools and individuals book and re-book it for its experience and knowledge of protocol.

services.name: Birthday, Anniversary & School Prom DJs
services.description: DJs for birthday and anniversary parties, with a wide music catalogue for guests of mixed ages and tastes. They also play school proms and school discos, with lighting that includes lasers.
services.more: For proms and school discos, the business says its DJs keep up with current music as well as the classics.

services.name: Ambience Uplighting
services.description: Colour uplighting to change the look of a venue. Their site shows before-and-after galleries in a range of colours at Broxbourne Golf Complex, Theydon Bois Golf Club and Ware Priory.
services.more: The business says most of its clients ask for uplighting. Its galleries show it used for an ambient guest arrival and in red and green for Christmas.

services.name: Dance Floors, Backdrops & Light-Up Letters
services.description: White LED dance floors, starlit or white LED backdrops for the DJ area, top table or ceremony, giant light-up LOVE letters and LED numbers, and DJ booth set-ups from Standard to Premier.
services.more: Set-ups include an all-white version of the Premier Set Up, with DJ booths in black or white, many with a starlit finish. In the Premier Lighting Set Up, the lighting units sit on podiums that can be lit in any colour instead of on traditional DJ stands.

services.name: Photo Booth, 360 Video Booth & Confetti
services.description: A deluxe photo booth or a 360 video booth for guests, which the business says comes with plenty of props. Confetti bombs can also be fired during the First Dance at weddings.
services.more: The business describes its booths as having 'more props than we have seen at anybody else's'.

identity.note: Some online listings give 2010 as a start date, but that appears to be when the business joined a directory: it says it has been in the DJ industry for over 30 years and does not publish a founding year.

howItWorks.title: Send a booking request
howItWorks.text: Use the booking form on the Tony Poole Discos website to request a date and share the details of your event.

howItWorks.title: Check the Reservation Form
howItWorks.text: The business records the event details and any special instructions on a Reservation Form and emails it over. Reply by email to confirm it is right, or send it back with amendments.

howItWorks.title: Pay the deposit
howItWorks.text: A deposit of 25% of the total event cost is generally payable within 14 days of confirming.

howItWorks.title: Plan the music
howItWorks.text: Send over the tracks and genres you would like, plus anything to avoid. Some clients choose most of the music, some make a few requests and some leave it all to the DJ; the business has no preference.

howItWorks.title: Settle the balance
howItWorks.text: The balance is paid on the night by cash or cheque, or beforehand by BACS transfer.

goodToKnow.text: If an event is cancelled within 14 days of the date, the business normally asks for a further payment of 25% of the total fee.
Without the All Day Service, the DJ sets up between the speeches and the evening party; the business says this typically takes about an hour.
The business may photograph or film events and use the images on its website and in advertising; anyone who would like an image removed can ask through the contact form.

faqs.q: Why do they ask for a list of songs not to play?
faqs.a: To avoid upsetting anyone. The business says first dances from previous marriages and tracks played at recent funerals increasingly need to be avoided.

faqs.q: Can they play a themed night?
faqs.a: Yes. All their DJs have the knowledge and back catalogue to play most types of themed night built around one genre or era, though at most events they mix genres to suit varied tastes.

faqs.q: Can the DJ cover the ceremony and speeches as well as the party?
faqs.a: Yes, through the All Day Service. The DJ can play the ceremony music through a mini PA if you marry at the reception venue, play background music through the drinks reception and meal, and amplify speeches with a wireless microphone.

faqs.q: Do they work alongside a Toastmaster?
faqs.a: Yes. The business says it is very happy to work with Toastmasters, and can provide a wireless microphone for one to use through its sound system.

faqs.q: Do they take Christmas bookings from venues?
faqs.a: Yes. In December they play both private company parties and venue or agency party nights, sometimes on block bookings, and venue event managers and social secretaries are invited to get in touch about seasonal packages.

toot-sweet-candy-cart.intro: Toot Sweet Candy Cart describes itself as a candy cart hire business in Chelmsford, Essex. They hire out a handmade Victorian candy cart, dressed with sweets and decorations, and offer a variety of sweet packages.
about: The cart itself is white, with spoked wheels and the business name painted on the front panel. Photos show it set up with balloon garlands, bunting, flowers, cakes, doughnuts and jars of sweets. Their round grey logo shows an illustrated cart and carries the words 'EST 2020', and their X account dates from March 2020.

In June 2020 they restyled the cart as a brunch and afternoon-tea display, saying they had 'tried something a little different with the Candy Cart'. The display had a Victoria sponge, scones, sandwiches, watermelon, champagne and a personalised 'On Weekends We Brunch' sign.

That same month, the business also made personalised sweet boxes. Each held 12 different sweets and Ferrero Rochers and came with a choice of colour theme and a personalised gift tag and message. The boxes were posted out, and free delivery was offered around Chelmsford and Ingatestone at the time. Their most recent visible public posts date from June 2020, so planners should check current availability, packages and pricing directly with the business, for example through their Facebook page.
